wstep: This card describes NCHFP pickled bell peppers in a vinegar, sugar and water brine, filled into sterile jars and processed in a boiling-water bath.

sekcje.naglowek: Why the recipe must not be changed
akapity: The whole product needs a minimum, uniform level of acid to prevent the growth of botulism bacteria.
Do not change the proportions of vinegar, vegetables and water, and do not use vinegar of unknown acidity; use only recipes with tested proportions.
For pickles, white distilled vinegar and cider vinegar with 5% acidity are recommended.
NCHFP uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml.

For about 9 pint jars NCHFP uses 7 pounds (about 3.2 kg) of firm bell peppers, 3 1/2 cups of sugar, 3 cups of vinegar with 5% acidity, 3 cups of water, 9 cloves of garlic and 4 1/2 teaspoons of canning or pickling salt.
NCHFP puts the empty jars right side up on the rack in a boiling-water canner and fills the canner and jars with hot (not boiling) water to 1 inch (about 2.5 cm) above the tops of the jars.
To sterilize empty jars, NCHFP boils them for 10 minutes below 1000 ft, and above that 1 minute longer for each additional thousand feet.
JarAtlas rule for metres: boil the jars for 10 minutes up to 300 m, and add 1 minute for every further 300 m or part of it.
Wash the peppers, cut them into quarters, remove the cores and seeds, cut away any blemishes and slice the peppers into strips.
Boil the sugar, vinegar and water for 1 minute, add the peppers and bring to a boil.
Remove and drain the hot sterilized jars one at a time, just before filling them.
Put 1/2 clove of garlic and 1/4 teaspoon of salt in each sterile half-pint jar, and double the amounts for pint jars.
Add the pepper strips and cover them with the hot vinegar mixture, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace.
Put on the lids and process.
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m) process half-pint and pint jars in a boiling-water bath for 5 minutes.
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased.
At 1001–6000 ft (above 300 m up to 1800 m) process half-pints and pints for 10 minutes.
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process half-pints and pints for 15 minutes.
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m.
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage.
The NCHFP table gives times only for half-pint and pint jars.
JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): a pint holds about 473 ml, so a 0.5 l jar has no tested time in this recipe; use jars of up to 473 ml.
